skill.name: skill-management
skill.description: Create, update, test, and organize Agent Skills for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill explains skill locations, frontmatter, safe tool limits, sharing, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Guides authors through creating, managing, sharing, and troubleshooting Agent Skills.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, and documented .claude/skills paths. No prompt injection, exfiltration intent, hidden persistence, or executable package code was found. The recursive deletion alert is overbroad because the example targets a named skill directory, but safer deletion wording would improve the guidance.

remediation.issue: Destructive removal example uses recursive forced deletion for a personal skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer safer deletion guidance, such as confirming the exact path first or moving the skill directory to a backup location.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear rules for creating and sharing Agent Skills. This skill provides practical guidance for structure, frontmatter, tool limits, updates, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains personal, project, and plugin skill locations.
Shows how to scaffold a new skill directory and SKILL.md file.
Defines required frontmatter fields and optional allowed-tools limits.
Describes single-file and multi-file skill layouts.
Covers listing, editing, removing, committing, and sharing skills.
Provides troubleshooting checks for activation, file paths, and YAML syntax.
limitations: Guidance is written primarily in Korean, with some English examples.
Examples target Claude skill directories and may need adaptation for other tools.
The skill does not include automated validators or test scripts.
Shell and Git examples require user review before execution.

use_cases.title: Create a personal skill
use_cases.description: An individual author can scaffold a focused skill with valid frontmatter and examples.

use_cases.title: Standardize project skills
use_cases.description: A development team can place shared skills under a project directory and commit them to Git.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot skill activation
use_cases.description: A support lead can check descriptions, paths, and YAML syntax when a skill does not trigger.

prompt_templates.title: Create my first skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner author creating a new skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill-management to help me create a personal Agent Skill for [task]. Include the directory plan, required frontmatter, and example instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a workflow into a skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate user turning a repeatable workflow into reusable guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill-management to convert my workflow into a focused skill. Recommend the name, description, allowed tools, sections, and examples.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a team skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Team lead publishing a project-level skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill-management to design a project skill for my team. Include folder placement, Git sharing steps, tool limits, and version notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced author preparing a skill for publication.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use skill-management to review my current skill folder for structure, frontmatter, allowed-tools, references, and troubleshooting risks. Provide prioritized changes.

output_examples.input: I need a personal skill for summarizing meeting notes.
output_examples.output: A concise plan with a skill name, description, folder location, required sections, and example usage guidance.

output_examples.input: Our team wants to share a code review skill.
output_examples.output: A project skill setup plan, Git sharing steps, and a frontmatter checklist for limited read-only tools.

output_examples.input: Claude does not select my skill.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering trigger wording, file naming, path placement, and YAML syntax checks.

best_practices: Keep each skill focused on one repeatable workflow.
Limit allowed tools to the minimum needed for the skill.
Include concrete examples and version history for shared skills.
anti_patterns: Creating one broad skill that covers unrelated workflows.
Using vague descriptions that do not include trigger context.
Running destructive shell examples without checking the target path.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Agent Skills with correct folders, frontmatter, instructions, examples, and tool limits.

faq.question: Can it manage both personal and project skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains personal skill folders, project skill folders, and plugin distribution context.

faq.question: Does it include safety guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows allowed-tools usage and recommends limiting tools for sensitive workflows.

faq.question: Is the guidance specific to Claude Code?
faq.answer: The examples target Claude skill conventions, but many structure practices also help Codex users.

faq.question: Does it run automated tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides authoring and troubleshooting guidance, not a test runner.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when creating, updating, sharing, removing, or debugging an Agent Skill.
